study_identification_part.si4_title: Gray matter atrophy is constrained by normal structural brain network architecture in depression

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Test whether individual-level gray matter atrophy patterns in depression are constrained by normal connectome architecture; identify patient-specific and shared disease epicenters; examine vulnerability of regions connected to epicenters and whether connectome–atrophy association reveals homogeneous subgroups.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: In-house cohort from First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper clearly describes two independent Chinese datasets collected at specific institutions. These are in-house cohorts rather than named public datasets.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Two independent datasets were included in this study: a discovery dataset and a replication dataset... The discovery dataset included 105 never-treated first-episode patients with depression and matched 130 healthy controls (HCs) recruited from the first out-patient services of Department of Psychiatry, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University... The replication dataset included 106 patients with depression and matched 126 HCs... recruited from the Clinical Hospital of Chengdu Brain Science Institute, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Structural multi-epicenter connectome profiles explain substantial variance in individual GMV atrophy in depression, highlighting shared epicenters (e.g., hippocampus, thalamus, medial frontal gyrus), greater vulnerability of strongly connected regions, and two subgroups differing in age of onset.
